dart.name: Dart
dart.intro: From your first variable to isolates, tooling and publishing packages. Open a stop to see what to learn, key concepts and official resources.

stages.title: Getting started
stages.blurb: Install the SDK, run code instantly in the browser and learn how a Dart program is structured.
stages.build: A command-line “hello, name” program that reads input.

topics.d: Install via the Flutter SDK or standalone and confirm with dart --version.
Write and run Dart in the browser with zero setup — ideal for experiments.
Every app starts at main(). Learn imports, libraries and comments.
Create, run, compile and format projects from the terminal.
How the same code runs as JIT, native AOT, JavaScript or Wasm.

stages.title: Language basics
stages.blurb: The building blocks: variables, types, operators, control flow, functions and errors.
stages.build: A tip calculator CLI with input validation.

topics.d: Declare with var, final and const, and understand type inference.
Numbers, strings, booleans, runes and symbols.
Arithmetic, equality, type tests, cascades and conditional expressions.
Branch and loop through your logic.
Functions are first-class objects with flexible parameters.
Throw, catch and clean up with exceptions.
Static typing with escape hatches: dynamic, Object and type aliases.
Chain operations on one object without temporaries.
Catch bad assumptions early in development builds.

stages.title: Collections
stages.blurb: Lists, sets and maps plus the modern syntax that makes data pleasant to shape.
stages.build: A to-do list CLI that adds, filters and groups tasks.

topics.d: The three core collection types and their literals.
Transform data with lazy iterable methods.
Build collections declaratively.
Anonymous, immutable aggregates for returning multiple values.
Destructure and match data structurally.
Order data and define natural ordering.
Prevent accidental mutation of shared data.

stages.title: Null safety
stages.blurb: Understand why the compiler stops you — and how to work with it, not against it.
stages.build: Refactor your to-do app to be fully null-safe without a single !.

topics.d: Types are non-nullable by default; add ? to allow null.
Safely read, default and assert values.
Defer initialisation while keeping non-null types.
How flow analysis narrows types after checks.

stages.title: Core libraries
stages.blurb: The standard library you will reach for every day: text, dates, maths, JSON and files.
stages.build: A CLI that reads a CSV file, aggregates it and writes JSON.

topics.d: Search, split and transform text.
Work with time without off-by-one surprises.
Random numbers, constants and geometry.
Encode and decode JSON, UTF-8 and Base64.
Files, directories, processes and HTTP on native platforms.
Build and parse URLs safely.

stages.title: Object-oriented Dart
stages.blurb: Model your domain with classes, mixins, sealed hierarchies and generics.
stages.build: A bank-account library with sealed transaction types.

topics.d: Fields, methods and the many kinds of constructors.
Extend classes and implement implicit interfaces.
Reuse behaviour across class hierarchies.
Add functionality to existing types.
Control how classes can be used and get exhaustive switches.
Enums with fields, methods and interfaces.
Write type-safe, reusable code.
Computed properties and controlled mutation.
Value equality for models and collections.
Define +, [] and friends on your own types.

stages.title: Type system & generics
stages.blurb: Go deeper into how Dart types work, so the analyzer becomes your ally.
stages.build: A generic, type-safe cache with expiry and typed keys.

topics.d: Reusable, type-safe building blocks.
Where Object?, dynamic, void and Never fit.
Describe callbacks precisely.
Why List<Cat> is a List<Animal>, and when that bites.
Zero-cost wrappers that give primitives a new API.
What the compiler infers and how to guide it.

stages.title: Async & concurrency
stages.blurb: Futures, streams and real parallelism with isolates.
stages.build: A CLI that fetches several URLs concurrently and streams progress.

topics.d: Represent a value that arrives later.
Write asynchronous code that reads top to bottom.
Sequences of async events.
Run CPU-heavy work in parallel without shared memory.
Advanced: intercept async errors and context.
How Dart schedules work on a single thread.
Bridge callback APIs and handle failures properly.

stages.title: Generators & streams in depth
stages.blurb: Produce values lazily and build reactive pipelines with streams.
stages.build: A live log tailer that filters, debounces and batches lines.

topics.d: Produce iterables lazily with yield.
Produce streams of values over time.
Map, filter and combine streams.
Choose the right subscription model.
Pause, resume and clean up subscriptions.
Extra reactive operators for complex flows.

stages.title: Design patterns
stages.blurb: Idiomatic ways to structure Dart code that stays readable as it grows.
stages.build: Restructure your CSV tool into repository, service and CLI layers.

topics.d: Prefer final fields and copyWith for predictable state.
Control instance creation.
Separate data access from business logic.
Pass dependencies in instead of reaching for globals.
Model failure explicitly with sealed classes.

stages.title: Tooling & quality
stages.blurb: The everyday toolchain: packages, lints, style and tests.
stages.build: Add tests and lints to your bank-account library and hit zero warnings.

topics.d: Declare dependencies and manage versions.
Catch bugs and enforce style statically.
Community conventions for style, docs and API design.
Unit tests with package:test and mocks.
Share a package with the world.
Breakpoints, the observatory and DevTools for Dart apps.
Write doc comments and generate API docs.
Measure before you optimise.

stages.title: Testing in depth
stages.blurb: Build a test suite you trust: structure, async, mocks and coverage.
stages.build: 90% coverage on your generic cache including async expiry.

topics.d: Organise tests that read like documentation.
Express expectations clearly.
Test futures, streams and timers deterministically.
Replace dependencies in tests.
Measure what your tests exercise.
Run tests on every push.

stages.title: Packages & libraries
stages.blurb: Organise code into libraries and packages others can depend on.
stages.build: Split your project into a reusable package plus an example app.

topics.d: Lay out a package the conventional way.
Split one library across files (mostly for codegen).
Different implementations per platform.
Semantic versioning and dependency resolution.
Manage monorepos with multiple packages.

stages.title: Networking & data
stages.blurb: Talk to the network and turn raw data into typed models.
stages.build: A typed client for a public REST API with retries and caching.

topics.d: Make HTTP requests across platforms.
Map JSON to models safely.
Advanced client features.
Two-way realtime connections.
Read and write large data efficiently.

stages.title: Performance
stages.blurb: Make Dart code fast and lean — and prove it with measurements.
stages.build: Profile your API client and cut its parse time in half.

topics.d: Why dev builds and release builds behave differently.
Free speed and memory from compile-time constants.
Find hot spots with DevTools.
Understand allocation and avoid leaks.
Keep the main isolate responsive.

stages.title: Going further
stages.blurb: Pick a direction: servers, CLIs, the web, code generation or native interop.
stages.build: A small REST API with shelf, or a CLI published to pub.dev.

topics.d: Parse arguments and build real tools.
Generate boilerplate with build_runner.
Build HTTP servers and APIs.
Call JavaScript from Dart compiled to the web.
Call native C libraries directly.
Share models between a Dart backend and a Flutter app.
Typed, efficient service APIs.
Compile Dart to Wasm for the web.

flutter.name: Flutter
flutter.intro: From hot reload to shipping on every store. Open a stop to see what to learn, key concepts and official resources.

stages.title: Dart essentials
stages.blurb: Flutter is written in Dart. Get comfortable with these before building UI — or take the Dart track first.
stages.build: Solve five small exercises in DartPad.

topics.d: Variables, functions, classes and collections.
Why ?, ! and late matter in every widget.
Load data without freezing the UI.
Modern Dart you will see in newer codebases.

stages.title: Setup & tooling
stages.blurb: Install Flutter, pick an editor and meet hot reload and DevTools.
stages.build: Run the counter app on a device and an emulator.

topics.d: Install the SDK and platform toolchains, then run flutter doctor.
VS Code or Android Studio with the Flutter plugin.
What lives in lib/, test/, platform folders and pubspec.yaml.
Iterate in sub-second loops while keeping state.
Inspect layouts, profile performance and debug memory.

stages.title: Widget fundamentals
stages.blurb: Everything is a widget. Learn how they compose, rebuild and hold state.
stages.build: A profile card screen built from scratch.

topics.d: When a widget needs state, and how setState triggers rebuilds.
How widgets, elements and render objects relate.
The building blocks you use every day.
Render long scrolling content efficiently.
The standard skeleton of a Material app.
When widgets are created, updated and disposed.

stages.title: Layout & responsive
stages.blurb: Understand constraints and build UIs that adapt from phones to desktops.
stages.build: A responsive dashboard that reflows from 1 to 3 columns.

topics.d: The three workhorses of layout.
“Constraints go down, sizes go up, parent sets position.”
Adjust layouts for screen size and input type.
Custom scroll effects with CustomScrollView.
Dialogs, sheets, snackbars and menus.
Respect notches, keyboards and system bars.

stages.title: Styling & assets
stages.blurb: Make it look right: Material 3, themes, fonts and images.
stages.build: Light and dark themes for your dashboard.

topics.d: Use the design systems built into Flutter.
Centralise colours and type with ThemeData.
Bundle images and load them at the right resolution.
Ship your own typefaces.

stages.title: Custom UI & graphics
stages.blurb: Go beyond stock widgets: paint, clip and render your own UI.
stages.build: A custom animated progress ring and a hand-drawn chart.

topics.d: Draw directly onto a canvas.
Shape and filter widgets.
Build reusable widgets with clean APIs.
GPU effects written in GLSL.
Custom layout and painting at the lowest level.

stages.title: Interaction & motion
stages.blurb: Respond to touch, keyboard and time.
stages.build: An animated onboarding flow with a validated sign-up form.

topics.d: Taps, drags and swipes.
Collect and validate user input.
Animate by changing a value.
Full control with controllers and tweens.
Interactive vector animations from a design tool.
Shortcuts, focus traversal and desktop-grade input.
Animate between screens.
Springs, flings and choreographed sequences.

stages.title: Navigation
stages.blurb: Move between screens, pass data and handle deep links.
stages.build: A multi-screen shop with tabs and deep links to products.

topics.d: Push and pop routes imperatively.
Declarative, URL-based routing.
Open specific screens from URLs.
Bottom tabs with independent back stacks.
Redirect based on auth or onboarding state.
The declarative Navigator 2.0 primitives underneath.

stages.title: State management
stages.blurb: Start with setState, understand InheritedWidget, then choose a pattern that scales.
stages.build: Refactor the shop’s cart to shared state with tests.

topics.d: Local state and passing it down.
The primitive most state libraries build on.
A simple, widely used wrapper around InheritedWidget.
Compile-safe providers that work outside the widget tree.
Event-driven state with clear separation.
Rebuild only what changes.
Trade-offs for team size, testability and scale.
Fine-grained reactive alternatives.

stages.title: Data & storage
stages.blurb: Talk to APIs, model JSON and keep data on the device.
stages.build: A news reader that caches articles for offline use.

topics.d: Fetch and send data over the network.
Serialise data safely.
Persist small settings.
Structured offline data with SQL.
Auth, Firestore and push notifications with little backend work.
Push data live from server to app.
Keep the app useful with no connection.
Postgres, auth and storage as a service.
Query exactly the data you need.

stages.title: Device features
stages.blurb: Reach the hardware: camera, location, notifications and background work.
stages.build: A photo journal with location tags and daily reminders.

topics.d: Ask for access the right way on each platform.
Capture and pick photos and video.
Get position and show maps.
Local and push notifications.
Run tasks when the app is not in the foreground.
Accelerometer, gyroscope and Face ID / fingerprint.

stages.title: Architecture & platform
stages.blurb: Structure apps that grow, reach native APIs and speak every language.
stages.build: Split the news reader into layers and add a second language.

topics.d: Separate UI, logic and data into clear layers.
Call native Kotlin/Swift code.
Translate and localise your app.
Make your app usable by everyone.
Wire services without globals.
Catch, report and diagnose failures in production.
Package native code for reuse.

stages.title: Security
stages.blurb: Protect user data, credentials and your app binary.
stages.build: Add secure login with token refresh to the photo journal.

topics.d: Sign users in with OAuth, OIDC or email.
Keep tokens and secrets out of plain text.
Never ship API keys in source control.
Make reverse engineering harder.
Defend against man-in-the-middle attacks.

stages.title: Testing & performance
stages.blurb: Prove it works and keep it at 60fps before you ship.
stages.build: Reach 70% coverage on the news reader and fix one jank issue.

topics.d: Test logic in isolation.
Pump widgets and interact with them headlessly.
Drive the full app on a device.
Find and fix jank, rebuilds and memory leaks.
Isolate units from their dependencies.
Catch visual regressions pixel by pixel.
Measure and shrink your binary.

stages.title: Ship it
stages.blurb: Package, automate and release to the world.
stages.build: Publish a beta to TestFlight and Play internal testing.

topics.d: Separate dev, staging and production builds.
Brand your app on every platform.
Build, test and deploy automatically.
Sign, upload and pass review.
Ship the same codebase beyond mobile.
Version and build numbers that stores accept.
Ship Dart fixes without a store review.

stages.title: Grow & maintain
stages.blurb: After launch: measure, monetise and keep the codebase healthy.
stages.build: Add analytics events and a paywall to one feature.

topics.d: Understand how people use your app.
Sell subscriptions and unlocks.
Know about problems before reviews do.
Stay current without breaking things.
Monetise with mobile ads.

stages.title: Specialise
stages.blurb: Pick a frontier. These are optional deep dives once the core is solid.
stages.build: A small game, an AI-assisted feature or a desktop companion app.

topics.d: A 2D game engine built on Flutter.
On-device ML and generative AI features.
Build for the browser: renderers, SEO and PWAs.
Windows, macOS and Linux apps.
Run Flutter on custom hardware.
Embed Flutter in an existing native app.
